items.title: New York City Cops Shut Down Haywire’s Times Square Pop-Up
items.summary:
The NYPD broke up an unannounced Haywire performance in Times Square on Wednesday night, cutting the Boston hardcore band off after a song and a half. The set was meant to double as a music video shoot, and it ended with officers clearing the crowd and confiscating the band's amplifiers.

Haywire announced the location roughly an hour beforehand on an Instagram story, posting a photo of the spot along with its latitude and longitude. A few hundred fans and friends turned up. According to Stereogum, the band's publicist said no one was arrested.

Setlist.fm logged the abbreviated performance: Haywire played "Flex Your Head," from the new album, then started into the singalong simply titled "Haywire." Police moved in during that second song, pushing moshers back and dispersing the crowd. One officer pulled the drumsticks directly out of the drummer's hands.

The guerrilla set fits the band's established pattern. Haywire built a following on relentless touring, surprise performances in places bands don't usually play, and last-minute additions to small regional bills.

The group released I Don't Wanna Say Goodbye earlier this month, their second album and first for Roadrunner, and had already shot videos for the singles "Interstate Love Affair" and "Sincerely Yours." The Times Square shoot was intended as another one, and the footage of the shutdown is likely more striking than a completed set would have been.

Haywire plays a pair of US festivals next month before heading to Australia for a tour. I Don't Wanna Say Goodbye is out now.

items.title: ‘Monarch: Legacy of Monsters’ Eyes Season 3 Renewal at Apple TV With New Writers, Showrunner
items.summary:
Apple TV and Legendary Television are negotiating a third season of Monarch: Legacy of Monsters, and the renewal would come with a substantially rebuilt creative team. Variety reported that a Season 3 would operate under a new showrunner with a new writing staff, and would introduce Titans not yet seen on the series.

According to an individual with knowledge of the talks, multiple candidates have been approached about taking over as showrunner. It remains unclear whether characters from the first two seasons would continue into a third.

Chris Black and Matt Fraction created the series, with Black serving as showrunner and executive producer on Season 2. Joby Harold and Tory Tunnell of Safehouse Pictures executive produce, alongside Jen Roskind, Matt Shakman, Lawrence Trilling and Andrew Colville on the second season. Hiro Matsuoka and Takemasa Arita executive produce for Toho Co., Ltd., which owns Godzilla.

The show premiered on Apple TV in 2023, with its second season arriving in February 2026. Its expansion continues regardless of the Season 3 outcome.

A spinoff centered on Wyatt Russell's Col. Lee Shaw remains in development, following the character in 1984 as he works to stop the Soviets from releasing a destructive new Titan. Harold will showrun that series and is developing several more projects inside Legendary's Monsterverse.

Beyond Russell, the spinoff cast includes Millie Brady, Pilou Asbæk, Corey Stoll, Ralph Ineson, Nyasha Hatendi, Connie Nielsen and Stana Katic. Apple has not announced a formal Season 3 order.

items.title: The Strokes’ Nick Valensi Joins Duran Duran In Paris
items.summary:
Nick Valensi, the Strokes guitarist currently on a break from the band, walked onstage with Duran Duran at the Accor Arena in Paris on Thursday night. He joined the group for "Rio," their 1982 hit, which closed the show.

The guest spot did not go smoothly. Stereogum reported that Valensi's guitar developed a technical problem, halting the performance for several minutes while Simon Le Bon improvised and stagehands worked on the instrument.

Valensi has a personal connection to the band through his wife, the photographer and television presenter Amanda de Cadenet, who was previously married to Duran Duran bassist John Taylor.

The appearance came the same week the Strokes played Dublin without him. Longwave's Steve Schlitz has filled Valensi's spot for the past several months, and the band's touring has continued in his absence.

Valensi played on the Strokes' new album Reality Awaits, and his last performance with the group was at Coachella in April. Julian Casablancas said last year that he and Valensi no longer speak. Neither Valensi nor the band has explained the break.

In the meantime, Valensi has been turning up as a guest elsewhere. He joined Jack White onstage at a Los Angeles show last month, and the Duran Duran cameo follows that pattern.
